findings.title: Double interpolation: queries are interpolated in runShardSplitQuery and again in runSplitQuery
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on each query (line 52), then passes the already-interpolated queries to splitQueriesByStreamShard, which calls runSplitQuery (line 163). runSplitQuery (querySplitting.ts line 299) also calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on its input targets. This means every query going through the shard splitting path is interpolated twice. If an interpolated variable value contains text that resembles a template variable (e.g., a label value containing `$`), the second interpolation pass could corrupt the query or produce unexpected results. The tests pass only because the mock replace function is idempotent on already-replaced strings, but real-world variable values may not be.

findings.title: Filtering by expr before interpolation changes behavior for variables that resolve to empty strings
findings.body: The previous code called interpolateVariablesInQueries first, then filtered by query.expr. The new code filters by query.expr first (line 50), then interpolates (line 52). If a query has expr set to a variable like '$myVar' that interpolates to an empty string, the old code would filter it out after interpolation, but the new code lets it through the filter (since '$myVar' is truthy) and then interpolates it to an empty string. This empty-expr query will then be passed downstream and potentially sent to the backend, causing errors or unexpected behavior. The same issue exists in querySplitting.ts line 298.
